Abstract
We study when a skip connection around a single-hidden-layer MLP can be absorbed into
a residual-free MLP of the same width. We first show that for any architecture whose
skip branch is an invertible linear map (including Hyper-Connections and their manifold-
constrained variants), the problem reduces to the identity skip case.
For homogeneous
activations of degree k ̸= 1, such as ReLU2 and ReGLU, absorption is unconditionally
impossible by a degree argument. For gated activations whose gate is differentiable at the
origin with g(0) = 0, including SwiGLU and GeGLU, a linearization argument gives the
same conclusion. These impossibility results extend to arbitrary depth: a composition of L
residual blocks using such activations cannot be replicated by any composition of L residual-
free blocks of the same width. For ungated ReLU and GELU, the situation is richer. For
generic weight matrices, absorption holds at the single-block level if and only if there exists
an index set S of size at least d such that Wdown[:, S] Wup[S, :] = −Id. This condition is
non-generic (it fails with probability one under continuous weight distributions), so skip-
connected and residual-free MLPs of the same width represent generically disjoint function
classes. Whether this disjointness persists for deep compositions of ReLU or GELU blocks
remains open.

1 Introduction
Skip connections were the breakthrough that enabled systematic training of deep neural
networks. Since their introduction by He et al. (2016a, 2016b), they have become present
in virtually every facet of state-of-the-art deep learning: the Transformer (Vaswani et al.,
2017), Vision Transformers (Dosovitskiy et al., 2021), ConvNeXt (Liu et al., 2022), LLaMA
(Touvron et al., 2023; Dubey et al., 2024), DeepSeek (DeepSeek-AI, 2024), and Gemma
(Gemma Team, 2024) all wrap every attention and MLP sub-layer in a branch x 7→x +
MLP(x).
Recent work has extended this pattern beyond the identity, replacing it with
learnable mixing matrices (Zhu et al., 2024; Xie et al., 2025). The prevailing understanding
is that skip connections smooth the loss landscape (Li et al., 2018) and help gradients flow
(He et al., 2016b; Xiong et al., 2020). We ask a different question: do skip connections
change what functions an MLP can represent?
Given a fixed MLP2(x) = Wdown σ(Wup x), when does there exist an MLP1(x) =
Vdown σ(Vup x) of the same width such that x+MLP2(x) = MLP1(x) for all inputs x? If such
absorption is possible, the skip connection is representationally redundant at that width. If
not, the skip connection grants access to a different region of function space. The converse
question is equally natural: can a residual-free MLP be rewritten as a skip-connected one?
Since the equation MLP1(x) = x + MLP2(x) rearranges to (−Id) x + MLP1(x) = MLP2(x),
both directions are instances of the same absorption problem, and our results settle both.
Contributions.
We show that when the skip branch is an invertible linear map, the ab-
sorption problem reduces to the identity skip case, covering Hyper-Connections and their
variants (Lemma 4). For homogeneous activations of degree k ̸= 1 (ReLU2, ReGLU), we
prove absorption is unconditionally impossible (Proposition 5), and we extend this to gated
activations whose gate is differentiable at the origin with g(0) = 0 (SwiGLU, GeGLU;
Shazeer 2020) via a linearization argument (Proposition 6).
These impossibility results

extend to compositions of arbitrary depth (Corollary 7), settling the question for the ac-
tivation functions used in current state-of-the-art models. For ungated ReLU and GELU,
we give if-and-only-if characterizations for generic weights at the single-block level (Theo-
rems 8 and 10), both reducing to the same submatrix condition Wdown[:, S] Wup[S, :] = −Id.
A corollary shows that skip-connected and residual-free MLPs are generically disjoint func-
tion classes (Corollary 11); we leave the multi-layer case for ReLU and GELU as an open
problem.
2 Related Work
Residual networks and reparametrization.
He et al. (2016a) introduced residual
connections and observed that they ease optimization in deep networks. A follow-up study
(He et al., 2016b) showed that placing the identity path outside all nonlinearities is critical
for training very deep ResNets. Subsequent work has studied the effect of skip connections
on the loss landscape (Li et al., 2018), on representational power (Lu et al., 2017), and
on implicit regularization (Hardt and Ma, 2017).
Our results complement this line by
characterizing exactly when the residual structure is algebraically redundant. Graef (2024)
and Karbevski and Mijoski (2025) studied weight elimination in skipless and skip-connected
transformers respectively; the latter provided a proof of the absorption characterization for
one activation. The present paper provides complete proofs for both ReLU and GELU, the
impossibility results for homogeneous and gated activations, and the general reduction to
the identity skip case.
The role of skip connections beyond optimization.
Ji et al. (2025) showed that self-
attention is uniquely dependent on skip connections for trainability: removing them from the
attention block causes catastrophic failure, while MLP blocks degrade more gracefully. This
asymmetry suggests that skip connections play different algebraic roles around different sub-
layers, a theme our work makes precise for the MLP case. On the analysis side, Elhage et al.
(2021) and Olsson et al. (2022) have studied the computational role of the residual stream in
transformers. Hyper-Connections (Zhu et al., 2024) and their manifold-constrained variants
(Xie et al., 2025) generalize the skip to a learnable mixing matrix; since these matrices are
generically invertible (Section 4), all our results apply.
Geometry of ReLU networks.
Arora et al. (2018) studied the reparametrization sym-
metries of deep ReLU networks, showing that positive rescaling of neurons preserves the
computed function. Montufar et al. (2014) analyzed the number of linear regions in deep
ReLU networks. Our necessity proof for the ReLU case builds on similar geometric ideas,
using the arrangement of kink hyperplanes to constrain the relationship between weight
matrices. For further background on functional equivalence of ReLU networks, see Phuong
and Lampert (2020).
Ridge functions and neural networks.
The uniqueness theorem for ridge function
representations (Pinkus, 2015, Chapter 3; Buhmann and Pinkus, 1999) provides the key
linear independence result used in our GELU proof. The connection between ridge function
theory and neural network expressivity has been explored by several authors; see, e.g.,
Pinkus (1999) and Kainen and K˚urkov´a (2010).

Problem setup.
The absorption question asks when a skip-connected MLP can be rewrit-
ten as a residual-free MLP of the same width. The answer differs sharply between gated
and ungated architectures: for gated MLPs, absorption is unconditionally impossible for all
weight matrices, so no measure-theoretic framework is needed. For ungated MLPs, exact
absorption is possible for special weight configurations but fails generically, and stating this
precisely requires equipping the parameter space with a measure.
Gated MLPs. Section 5 considers a gated architecture.

4 Reduction to the Identity Skip
Modern architectures do not always use a pure identity skip. In Hyper-Connections (Zhu
et al., 2024) and their manifold-constrained variants (Xie et al., 2025), the skip branch is
replaced by a learnable linear map M, yielding blocks of the form
M x + Wdown σ(Wup x).
(4)
The following lemma shows that when M is invertible, the absorption problem for (4)
reduces to the standard identity skip case.

R applied coordinatewise. For any Wup, Vup ∈RN×d and Wdown, Vdown ∈Rd×N,

5 Impossibility for Modern Activations
For the activation functions used in current state-of-the-art models, absorption is uncon-
ditionally impossible. We establish this through two complementary arguments: a homo-
geneity argument covering ReLU2 (So et al., 2022), used in the Nemotron family (NVIDIA,
2025) and the modded-nanogpt codebase (Jordan et al., 2024); and a Taylor expansion
argument covering the gated activations SwiGLU and GeGLU (Shazeer, 2020): SwiGLU is
used in LLaMA (Touvron et al., 2023; Dubey et al., 2024), DeepSeek (DeepSeek-AI, 2024),
Mistral (Jiang et al., 2023), and Qwen (Qwen Team, 2024); GeGLU in Gemma (Gemma
Team, 2024).

Both impossibility results extend from single blocks to compositions of arbitrary depth.
Corollary 7 (Depth extension) Let d ≥1, N ≥d, and L ≥1. Let σ be either homoge-
neous of degree k > 1 (applied coordinatewise) or a gated activation with g differentiable at
the origin and g(0) = 0. Consider a composition of L residual blocks
F(x) = fL ◦· · · ◦f1(x),
fi(x) = x + MLPi(x),
and a composition of L residual-free blocks
H(x) = hL ◦· · · ◦h1(x),
hi(x) = MLP′
i(x),
all of width N. Then F ̸= H.
Proof
In both cases, the MLP output satisfies MLP(x) = O(∥x∥2) near the origin. For
the residual composition, the degree-1 Taylor term passes through every block unchanged:
the Jacobian of fi at the origin is Id, so the Jacobian of F at the origin is Id. For the
residual-free composition, the Jacobian of each hi at the origin is 0 (since the MLP has no
linear term), so the Jacobian of H at the origin is 0. These cannot agree.
This settles the absorption question at arbitrary depth for every activation function used
in current state-of-the-art models: ReLU2, ReGLU, SwiGLU, and GeGLU. A deep residual
network using any of these activations cannot be replicated by a deep residual-free network
of the same depth and width.
The remainder of the paper addresses the case where absorption is sometimes possible:
ungated activations whose parity structure is compatible with degree 1.

8 Generic Disjointness of Function Classes
The submatrix condition Wdown[:, S] Wup[S, :] = −Id imposes d2 polynomial constraints
on the weights. Since there are only finitely many subsets S, the set of parameters in Θ
satisfying the condition for some S has Lebesgue measure zero. This yields the following.
Corollary 11 (Generic disjointness) Let d ≥2, N ≥d, and σ be ReLU or GELU. For
Lebesgue-almost every (Wup, Wdown) ∈RN×d × Rd×N, there exist no matrices Vup ∈RN×d
and Vdown ∈Rd×N such that
Wdown σ(Wup x) + x = Vdown σ(Vup x)
∀x ∈Rd.
In other words, for Lebesgue-almost every parameter in Θ, the corresponding element
of Fskip does not belong to Fff, and vice versa. The two families are generically disjoint,
intersecting only on a measure-zero set in parameter space.

9 Discussion
Ungated activations and the parity condition.
The identical algebraic condition in
Theorems 8 and 10 is not a coincidence. Both ReLU and GELU admit parity decompositions
whose odd part is exactly z/2.
Any ungated activation σ(z) with the property σ(z) −
σ(−z) = z will yield the same submatrix condition for identity absorption, provided the
even part E(z) = (σ(z) + σ(−z))/2 generates linearly independent ridge functions for non-
collinear directions. Ungated SiLU/Swish σ(z) = z/(1+e−z) satisfies this condition, though
it is rarely used without gating in practice.
Gated activations.
The dominant modern architecture uses gated MLPs: SwiGLU in
LLaMA (Touvron et al., 2023; Dubey et al., 2024), DeepSeek (DeepSeek-AI, 2024), Mistral
(Jiang et al., 2023), and Qwen (Qwen Team, 2024); GeGLU in Gemma (Gemma Team,
2024). Proposition 6 shows that absorption is unconditionally impossible for all of these.
Combined with Proposition 5 (which covers ReLU2 and ReGLU), this means that among ac-
tivations deployed at scale, only ungated GELU (GPT-2; Radford et al., 2019) and ungated
ReLU admit non-trivial absorption, and even then only non-generically.
Open problem: deep compositions with ReLU and GELU.
Corollary 7 settles
the multi-layer question for homogeneous and gated activations. For ungated ReLU and
GELU, the single-block characterization (Theorems 8 and 10) does not extend to depth in
the same way. The degree argument fails because ungated ReLU and GELU have a linear
term (z/2) in their Taylor expansion, so each residual-free block has a nonzero Jacobian
at the origin, and a composition of L such blocks can produce a nontrivial linear map.
Whether a composition of L residual ReLU or GELU blocks can always be matched by a
composition of L residual-free blocks of the same width remains open.

Can an MLP Absorb Its Own Skip Connection?
Rank-deficient mixing matrices.
Lemma 4 assumes M is invertible. If rank(M) = r <
d, write the SVD M = U diag(σ1, . . . , σr, 0, . . . , 0) V ⊤. In rotated coordinates y = V ⊤x,
the equation decomposes: on the first r coordinates, the skip has nonzero coefficients σi
and can be normalized to identity by absorbing σ−1

into the output projections, reducing
to the standard form. On the remaining d −r coordinates, the skip connection vanishes
and the equation asks when two MLPs compute the same function on that subspace. For
homogeneous activations of degree k ̸= 1 (Proposition 5), the degree argument applies to
any x /∈ker(M), so absorption remains impossible whenever M ̸= 0.
Structural implications.
The condition Wdown[:, S] Wup[S, :] = −Id requires |S| ≥d
neurons whose weights produce a rank-d factorization of −Id. In networks with large hidden
dimension (N ≫d), the number of candidate subsets S grows, but the condition remains a
measure-zero event under continuous weight distributions. This means that a residual MLP
block generically cannot be rewritten as a single feedforward map of the same width: the
skip connection accesses a different region of function space, not merely a reparametrization
of the same region. Any method that attempts to represent a skip-connected block as a
residual-free network must either increase width or accept approximation error.
Approximate absorption and future work.
Since exact absorption is non-generic
for ReLU and GELU, and impossible for all other activations considered here, a natural
question is how well approximate absorption can perform: given a skip-connected MLP, how
closely can a residual-free MLP of the same width approximate it? Karbevski and Mijoski
(2025) present experiments in this direction for the GELU activation. A systematic study
of the approximation error as a function of width, depth, activation, and weight structure
remains an important direction for future work.

Abstract: We study when a skip connection around a single-hidden-layer MLP can be absorbed into a residual-free MLP of the same width. We first show that for any architecture whose skip branch is an invertible linear map (including Hyper-Connections and their manifold- constrained variants), the problem reduces to the identity skip case. For homogeneous activations of degree k ̸= 1, such as ReLU2 and ReGLU, absorption is unconditionally impossible by a degree argument. For gated activations whose gate is differentiable at the origin with g(0) = 0, including SwiGLU and GeGLU, a linearization argument gives the same conclusion. These impossibility results extend to arbitrary depth: a composition of L residual blocks using such activations cannot be replicated by any composition of L residual- free blocks of the same width. For ungated ReLU and GELU, the situation is richer. For generic weight matrices, absorption holds at the single-block level if and only if there exists an index set S of size at least d such that Wdown[:, S] Wup[S, :] = −Id. This condition is non-generic (it fails with probability one under continuous weight distributions), so skip- connected and residual-free MLPs of the same width represent generically disjoint function classes. Whether this disjointness persists for deep compositions of ReLU or GELU blocks remains open.
